stories.title: Trump suspends Russian sanctions to keep peace talks alive
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that he blocked several sanctions on Russia on Friday night, two days before they were set to take effect, saying the action was meant to keep Moscow at the negotiating table in the Russia‑Ukraine war. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a “historic mistake.” Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called the suspension an “important and truly historic moment” and said the sanctions would have caused serious damage to the U.S. and global markets.
stories.why: The suspension may alter diplomatic leverage and economic pressure in the ongoing Russia‑Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: Overnight attack on St Petersburg oil terminal and depot kills one, injures five
stories.summary: An overnight strike hit the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot, killing at least one person and injuring at least five. Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at both sites. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia has struck Ukraine’s energy sector 76 times since a U.S. “energy ceasefire” was announced, and Ukraine paused its own strikes for three days before resuming them earlier this week.
stories.why: The attack hits facilities that fund Russia’s war effort and signals continued escalation in targeting energy infrastructure.
stories.previousTitle: Overnight attack kills one, injures five at two St Petersburg oil facilities
stories.previousSummary: At least one person was killed and five injured when an overnight strike hit the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot, with fires being extinguished after the attack. Governor Alexander Beglov confirmed the damage, while Kyiv had not yet commented. stories.title: Jio Platforms and Paras Healthcare set to launch large IPOs this week
stories.summary: Jio Platforms is preparing a ₹30,213‑crore initial public offering scheduled for October 21. Paras Healthcare will follow with its own ₹1,450‑crore IPO later in the week. Companies whose offerings closed last week—including Vaibhav Vyapaar, Ravita Engineering Services and Shellz India—are expected to begin trading on the stock exchanges during the same period.
stories.why: The offerings increase primary‑market activity and bring substantial new capital to Indian equity markets.
stories.previousTitle: Jio Platforms and Paras Healthcare IPOs open Oct 21, driving busy week in Indian market
stories.previousSummary: Reliance Jio Platforms is launching an IPO worth Rs 30,213 crore and Paras Healthcare is issuing Rs 1,450 crore of shares, both scheduled to open on October 21. In the same week, nine additional companies will list on Indian exchanges, with six on the mainboard and three on SME platforms. The cluster of offerings makes the primary market unusually active.

stories.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
stories.summary: Anthropic announced on Oct. 18 that it will create a “public benefit fund” by committing 5% of its shares to a wholly‑owned entity within the company, with an option to add another 2% for every 50% rise in Anthropic’s value. The fund may be used for large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations, and the company notes it has already pledged $200 million to study AI’s impact on the job market.
stories.why: The move addresses mounting public concern about AI and gives Anthropic a flexible mechanism to fund societal‑benefit projects.

stories.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to visit India for investment and energy talks
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to travel to India next week for meetings in Mumbai and Jamnagar. The discussions will centre on investment and energy issues. The visit occurs while the United States and India continue to experience delays in finalising a bilateral trade agreement, which the source attributes to a number of ongoing challenges.
stories.why: The outcome may affect progress on the stalled US‑India trade agreement.
stories.previousTitle: US‑India trade talks face delays ahead of Secretary Rubio’s visit
stories.previousSummary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India next week for meetings in Mumbai and Jamnagar on investment and energy. The United States and India have experienced considerable delays in finalising a trade agreement, which the source attributes to several ongoing challenges. The visit is intended to discuss ways to move the trade talks forward.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.
